nodes.name: Theorem 5
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{X,Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a causal $\mathrm{DAG}$, $\mathrm{CPDAG}$, $\mathrm{MAG}$ or $\mathrm{PAG}$ $\mathcal{G}$. Then $\mathbf{Z}$ is an adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in~$\mathcal{G}$ (see Definition~1) if and only if $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the generalized adjustment criterion relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in~$\mathcal{G}$ (see Definition~4).

nodes.name: Lemma 9
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{X,Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a $\mathrm{CPDAG}$ $(\mathrm{PAG})$ $\mathcal{G}$. If $\mathcal{G}$ is amenable relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$, then the following statements are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
\item $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the forbidden set condition\xspace (see Definition~4) relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in~$\mathcal{G}$.
\item  $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the forbidden set condition\xspace relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in every $\mathrm{DAG}$ $(\mathrm{MAG})$ in $[\mathcal{G}]$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Lemma 8
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ be disjoint node sets in a $\mathrm{CPDAG}$ $(\mathrm{PAG})$ $\mathcal{G}$. If $\mathcal{G}$ is amenable (see Definition~4) relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$, then every $\mathrm{DAG}$ $(\mathrm{MAG})$ in $[\mathcal{G}]$ is amenable relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$. On the other hand, if $\mathcal{G}$ violates the amenability condition\xspace{} relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$, then there is no adjustment set relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in~$\mathcal{G}$ (see Definition~1).

nodes.name: Lemma 49
nodes.statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be distinct nodes in a $\mathrm{PAG}$ $\mathcal{P}$ such that there is a possibly directed path ${p}^{*}$ from $X$ to $Y$ in~$\mathcal{P}$ that does not start with a visible edge out of $X$. Then there is a $\mathrm{MAG}$ $\mathcal{M}$ in $[\mathcal{P}]$ such that the path $p$ in~$\mathcal{M}$, consisting of the same sequence of nodes as ${p}^{*}$ in~$\mathcal{P}$, contains a subsequence $p'$ that is a directed path from $X$ to $Y$ starting with an invisible edge in~$\mathcal{M}$. In other words, $\mathcal{M}$ violates the amenability condition\xspace{} relative to $({X,Y})$.

nodes.name: Lemma 10
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{X,Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a $\mathrm{CPDAG}$ $(\mathrm{PAG})$ $\mathcal{G}$. If $\mathcal{G}$ is amenable relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$, and $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the forbidden set condition\xspace{} relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$, then the following statements are equivalent:
   \begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
\item $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the blocking condition\xspace{} (see Definition~4) relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in~$\mathcal{G}$.
\item  $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the blocking condition\xspace{} relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in every $\mathrm{DAG}$ $(\mathrm{MAG})$ in $[\mathcal{G}]$.
\item $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfies the blocking condition\xspace{} relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in a $\mathrm{DAG}$ $\mathcal{D}$ $(\mathrm{MAG} \mathcal{M})$ in $[\mathcal{G}]$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Lemma 52
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{X,Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a $\mathrm{PAG}$ $(\mathrm{CPDAG})$ $\mathcal{P}$.  Let $\mathcal{P}$ be amenable relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ and let $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfy the forbidden set condition\xspace{} relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in~$\mathcal{P}$. Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a $\mathrm{MAG}$ $(\mathrm{DAG})$ in $[\mathcal{P}]$ and let $p$ be a path with minimal $distance-from-\!{\mathbf{Z}}$ among the shortest proper non-causal paths from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ that are m-connecting given $\mathbf{Z}$ in~$\mathcal{M}$. Let ${p}^{*}$ in $\mathcal{P}$ be the corresponding path to $p$ in $\mathcal{M}$. Then ${p}^{*}$ is a proper definite status non-causal path from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ that is m-connecting given $\mathbf{Z}$ in~$\mathcal{P}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 51
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{X,Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a $\mathrm{PAG}$ $(\mathrm{CPDAG})$ $\mathcal{P}$.  Let $\mathcal{P}$ be amenable relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ and let $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfy the forbidden set condition\xspace{} relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in~$\mathcal{P}$. Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a $\mathrm{MAG}$ $(\mathrm{DAG})$ in $[\mathcal{P}]$ and let $p$ be a shortest proper non-causal path from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ that is m-connecting given $\mathbf{Z}$ in~$\mathcal{M}$. Let ${p}^{*}$ in~$\mathcal{P}$ be the corresponding path to $p$ in $\mathcal{M}$. Then ${p}^{*}$ is a proper definite status non-causal path in~$\mathcal{P}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 50
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{X,Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ be pairwise disjoint node sets in a $\mathrm{PAG}$ $(\mathrm{CPDAG})$ $\mathcal{P}$. Let $\mathcal{P}$ be amenable relative to $(\mathbf{X,Y})$ and let $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfy the forbidden set condition\xspace{} relative to $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ in~$\mathcal{P}$. Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a $\mathrm{MAG}$ $(\mathrm{DAG})$ in $[\mathcal{P}]$ and let $p = \langle X = V_{0}, V_{1},\dots ,V_{n} = Y \rangle, n \ge 2$, be a proper non-causal path from $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{Y}$ that is m-connecting given $\mathbf{Z}$ in~$\mathcal{M}$. Let ${p}^{*}$ in~$\mathcal{P}$ denote the path corresponding to $p$ in~$\mathcal{M}$. Then:

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Let $i,j \in \mathbb{N}, 0 < i < j \leq n$ such that there is an edge $\langle V_i, V_j \rangle$ in~$\mathcal{P}$. The path $ {p}^{*}(X,V_i) \oplus \langle V_i, V_j \rangle \oplus {p}^{*}(V_j,Y)$ (${p}^{*}(V_j, Y)$ is possibly of zero length) is a proper non-causal path in~$\mathcal{P}$. For $j=i+1$, this implies that ${p}^{*}$ is a proper non-causal path.
\item If $V_1$ is not of definite status on ${p}^{*}$, then $\langle X,V_2 \rangle \oplus {p}^{*}(V_2,Y)$, (${p}^{*}(V_2, Y)$ is possibly of zero length) exists and is a proper non-causal path in~$\mathcal{P}$.
\item If $n \ge 3$ and $V_k, 2 \leq k < n$ is not of definite status on ${p}^{*}$, and every non-endpoint node on ${p}^{*}(X,V_k)$ is a collider on ${p}^{*}$ and a parent of $V_{k+1}$ in~$\mathcal{M}$, then $\langle X,V_{k+1} \rangle \oplus {p}^{*}(V_{k+1},Y)$, (${p}^{*}(V_{k+1}, Y)$ is possibly of zero length) exists and is a proper non-causal path in~$\mathcal{P}$.
\end{enumerate}
